definitions.gloss: easy-going; taking the easy way out
definitions.explanation: Approaching things in a lazy or overly simplistic manner, without proper consideration or effort. Often has a negative connotation.
Something that can be done without difficulty (less common, more neutral usage).

examples.japanese: {安易|あんい}な{考|かんが}えは{危険|きけん}だ。
{安易|あんい}に{答|こた}えを{出|だ}すべきではない。
examples.english: You shouldn't come to a conclusion too easily.

examples.japanese: {安易|あんい}な{道|みち}を{選|えら}んではいけない。
examples.english: You shouldn't take the easy way out.

notes:
USAGE: Often used critically to describe someone who takes shortcuts or doesn't think carefully.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{安易|あんい}な{考|かんが}え (simplistic thinking)
・{安易|あんい}な{方法|ほうほう} (the easy way)
・{安易|あんい}に + verb (too easily, without proper thought)

NUANCE: Usually implies criticism - that something was done too casually or without sufficient care.

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{簡単|かんたん} - easy, simple (neutral)
・{楽|らく} - easy, comfortable (neutral/positive)
・{軽率|けいそつ} - careless, rash (negative)
